## Historical audit — S0157, visible chunk 1 of 6

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C2/test/commons_16007442/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. No reference or rendered image is visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — student request, line 1 | Reconstruct an indoor photograph as editable, multipart SceneAct/Blender geometry, matching camera, framing, materials and occlusion. The inferred goal is visual fidelity; it is not itself evidence of achieving it. |
| Initial build — student response line 3; execute step 1, line 4 | The student described an electronics workbench and supplied a complete program, not an empty patch. It creates multiple assets: bench, walls, cabinets, monitor, oscilloscope, meters, keyboard, lamp, soldering equipment, tools and cables. These are coded identities, not independent confirmation of the photograph. |
| Scene construction — line 4 | Colored primitive surfaces, roughness and blue-screen emission are specified; no image texture is used in the visible code. Multipart groups include lamp arms, hinge and shade; the upright meter is tilted as a unit, and keyboard and other objects are rotated. Grouping and intended connections do not establish correct physical contact or pose. Camera position, target and 45 mm lens, two area emitters and world illumination are specified. |
| Execution — execution_result step 1, line 5 | `ok: true`, no reported error; the log reports 16/16 samples, a saved `final.png` and `scene.blend`. Lines 6–7 record selection of step 1. This is **technical success for the first build**, not visual or geometric verification. |
| Autonomous review — student request line 8; student response line 10 | The student received the reference and step-1 render for a requested visual audit. Its own estimates describe reversed perspective, an exposed region below the desk, a small monitor, thin/high lamp and washed-out illumination. These are student visual judgments, not independently checked here. It proposed reversing camera X, extending the desktop, resizing/repositioning the monitor and shade, and reducing the main light. Line 11 again selects step 1; no execution of those proposals is visible in this chunk. |
| Teacher input | No teacher message, detection, diagnosis or proposed update is visible. The audit request is user/runner input, not evidence of a teacher intervention or its adoption. |

**Outcome and uncertainty.** The visible first execution succeeded and produced a render; overall reconstruction quality and final trajectory outcome are **unknown**. The images and remaining five chunks are unavailable, so actual object appearance, material fidelity, part connections, camera alignment, lighting issues and any later revision cannot be verified. The student's source-check statement and visual diagnosis are claims, not independent tests. The step-1 selection events do not prove final submission.

**Lessons.** Transferably, a successful render and a visual residual analysis answer different questions; proposed corrections require a subsequent execution and comparison to establish their effect. Task-specific hypotheses here concern camera direction, foreground desk extent, monitor/lamp proportions and light intensity. Their causal correctness and any improvement remain unresolved.
